comment_letters.staff_ask: Because Keytruda was 46% of 2024 revenue, staff asked Merck to file the Keytruda license agreements as exhibits or explain why it is not substantially dependent on them.
comment_letters.company_answer: Merck said it owns all rights to pembrolizumab, so it is not dependent on the two royalty-bearing licenses (6.5% falling to 2.5% in 2024 and ending 12/31/2026; plus 2% expiring by country), and filed nothing.
comment_letters.next_filing_disclosure: FY2025 10-K repeats the same royalty language (6.5% to 2.5%, through 2026, also applies to Keytruda Qlex; 2% royalty expired US Sep 2024 and major EU 2H25 but continues elsewhere); no agreement filed.
comment_letters.next_filing_cite: data/corpus/companies/MRK/10k_FY2025.md pdf 56 / printed 54; prior year data/corpus/companies/MRK/10k_FY2024.md pdf 55 / printed 53
comment_letters.why_it_matters: Royalty terms on the single product that is ~half of revenue sit in an MD&A paragraph, and the 2.5% royalty roll-off at end-2026 is a cost-of-sales tailwind that partly offsets Keytruda's 2028 LOE narrative.
comment_letters.impact_estimate: Estimate: 2.5% x ~$29-31B Keytruda sales = ~$0.7-0.8B/yr lower royalty expense from 2027 (Keytruda 2024 sales derived from 46% x total revenue; check product table).
comment_letters.staff_quote: We note that Keytruda accounted for 46% of your revenues in 2024. Please either file these agreements pursuant to Item 601(b)(10)(ii)(B) of Regulation S-K or explain why you believe your are not substantially dependent on licensing agreements providing you with the right to sell Keytruda.
comment_letters.reply_quote: As the Company owns all rights to Keytruda and does not rely on these agreements for its use or sale, the Company is not substantially dependent on any of these agreements and therefore does not believe that it is required to file any of these agreements pursuant to Item 601(b)(10)(ii)(B) of Regulation S-K.
